headline: [VERIFIED FACT -- the update] UAE-based Dana Gas, joint operator of the Khor Mor gas field, says production remains suspended
dek: [VERIFIED FACT -- the update] UAE-based Dana Gas, joint operator of the Khor Mor gas field, says production remains suspended following a 'suspected drone attack' on Sunday evening; the attack caused a fire, now extinguished. More than 70 percent of northern Iraq's Kurdish region is without power.
sources: Dana Gas statement via Al Jazeera liveblog
fault_line: Who hit Khor Mor -- and how many times can Kurdistan lose power before the Iran war's spillover becomes the story?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- the update] UAE-based Dana Gas, joint operator of the Khor Mor gas field, says production remains suspended following a 'suspected drone attack' on Sunday evening; the attack caused a fire, now extinguished. More than 70 percent of northern Iraq's Kurdish region is without power. [From 0300-01] An explosive-laden drone struck the field in Chamchamal, Sulaymaniyah province, late Sunday ~23:00, cutting ~2,800 MW (about two-thirds of Kurdistan power) and gas supplies to five power stations; no casualties per Iraq's PM initial assessment; no claim of responsibility.
sections.what_verified: Dana Gas statement relayed by Al Jazeera; the attack itself was corroborated at 0300-01 (Reuters/Kurdistan 24/Al Jazeera Baghdad reporting).
sections.what_disputed: No group has claimed responsibility. Erbil previously blamed Iran-aligned factions for past Khor Mor attacks, but no evidence has been presented for this one; the 0600-03 triage noted Kurdish authorities turning to hydropower to keep hospitals online.
sections.why_matters: The drone that cut 2,800 MW: Kurdistan's lights are still out, the gas is still off, and nobody has claimed the strike.
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW UPDATE to totw-20261109-0300-01 -- Dana Gas: production still suspended at Khor Mor after drone attack; fire extinguished; >70% of Kurdistan without power

totw_analysis: Our read: The drone that cut 2,800 MW: Kurdistan's lights are still out, the gas is still off, and nobody has claimed the strike. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Who hit Khor Mor -- and how many times can Kurdistan lose power before the Iran war's spillover becomes the story?
